# Homey Apps SDK v3 types

TypeScript declarations for the [Homey Apps SDK v3](https://apps.developer.homey.app/), generated from the SDK's
source. The API reference is at https://apps-sdk-v3.developer.homey.app/.

## Installation

Install the package under the `@types/homey` alias, so that `import Homey from 'homey'` and augmentations such as
`declare module 'homey'` resolve to these declarations:

```bash
npm install --save-dev @types/homey@npm:homey-apps-sdk-v3-types
```

Running `homey app add-types` in your app's folder does the same.

### `@types/node`

Homey runs apps on Node.js 22, so use `@types/node` 22. With newer `@types/node` majors, some checks, such as
misspelled event names, are silently skipped.

```bash
npm install --save-dev @types/node@22
```

## Typing your app

### `this.homey.app`

`this.homey.app` is typed as the base `App` class. To give it your own app's type, declare it once, anywhere in your
project:

```ts
import type MyApp from './app';

declare module 'homey' {
  interface HomeyTypes {
    app: MyApp;
  }
}
```

### Your own events

Event names and listener arguments are checked. `App`, `Driver` and `Device` don't emit events of their own, so an
app that emits its own events on them declares those events once, anywhere in its project:

```ts
import 'homey/events';

declare module 'homey/events' {
  interface DeviceEventMap {
    'reading': [value: number, unit: 'W' | 'kWh'];
    // Dynamic event names can use a template literal pattern
    [event: `webhook:${string}`]: [body: { text: string }];
  }
}
```

`AppEventMap` and `DriverEventMap` work the same way. Without such a declaration, `this.on('my-event', …)` fails with
*"Argument of type '…' is not assignable to parameter of type 'never'"*.

## Upgrading from 0.3.x

Version 1.x of these types is generated from the SDK itself and is much stricter than 0.3.x. Update the alias first,
since a `^0.3.x` range won't pick up 1.x:

```bash
npm install --save-dev @types/homey@npm:homey-apps-sdk-v3-types@^1
```

Changes you may need to make:

- **Typing `this.homey.app`:** if you augmented the `Homey` interface to give `app` your own type (e.g.
  `interface Homey extends … { app: MyApp }`), replace that with `HomeyTypes`, as shown above.
- **Your own events** on `App`, `Driver` or `Device` must be declared, as shown above.
- **Callbacks that return nothing:** the source passed to `Image#setStream()` and WebRTC keep-alive listeners must return
  nothing or a promise of nothing. Use a block body or the `void` operator for arrow functions that would return a
  value, e.g. `image.setStream(stream => void res.body.pipe(stream))`.
- **`super.onInit()` and other hooks** may now return either nothing or a promise, so use
  `await super.onInit()` instead of `super.onInit().then(…)`. In return, your own `onInit()`, `onUninit()`,
  `onPairListDevices()`, `ZigBeeNode#handleFrame` and pair session handlers no longer have to be `async`.
- **`LedringAnimation.Frame`** is now one complete frame: an array of 24 pixels. Use `LedringAnimation.Pixel` for a
  single LED.
- **Geolocation getters** (`getLatitude()`, `getLongitude()`, `getAccuracy()`, `getMode()`) return `null` when the
  location isn't available, for example without the `homey:manager:geolocation` permission.
- **Index signatures:** `Homey.env`, `getData()`, `getStore()` and `getSettings()` are `Record<string, …>`. With the
  `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` compiler options, use bracket access and handle
  `undefined`, e.g. `Homey.env['CLIENT_ID']`.
- **Z-Wave reports** are emitted by the command class, not by the node: listen with
  `node.CommandClass['COMMAND_CLASS_BASIC']?.on('report', …)`, not `node.on('report', …)`.
- **Renamed types:** `Widget.SettingAutocompleteResults`/`SettingAutocompleteCallback` are now
  `WidgetSettingAutocompleteResults`/`WidgetSettingAutocompleteCallback`, and `ManagerSpeechInput.Chunk`, `Location`,
  `Time` and `Word` are now `SpeechChunk`, `SpeechLocation`, `SpeechTime` and `SpeechWord`. The old names still work,
  but are deprecated. `FlowToken.Image` and `FlowCardTriggerDevice.Device` are gone: use `Homey.Image` and
  `Homey.Device`.

Some checks are new and may surface existing mistakes, for example a `createToken()` initial value that doesn't
match the token's `type`, or a widget autocomplete result without a `name`.
